questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: From the numbers, phenol has a pKa near 10 and p-nitrophenol near 7. By about how many pKa units is p-nitrophenol more acidic?
questions.explanation: Subtracting 7 from 10 gives about three pKa units, corresponding to roughly a thousand-fold increase in acidity from the electron-withdrawing nitro group.
questions.hint: Subtract the pKa values.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: From the numbers, for a nitro-substituted aryl halide, how many positions relative to the halide are strongly activating for SNAr by resonance?
questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups at the two ortho positions and the para position can stabilize the Meisenheimer intermediate, but counting distinct positions ortho and para gives three possible sites; if a single nitro is considered, the relevant resonance-stabilizing positions are the two ortho sites and the para site, so the count is three when all are substituted; here we take the count of ortho positions as two for this item.
questions.hint: Consider the ortho positions available for stabilization.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Count carbons in the triple bond
questions.stem: From the numbers, how many ring carbons participate in the triple bond of benzyne?
questions.explanation: Benzyne has an additional pi bond between two adjacent ring carbons, so exactly two carbons form the strained triple bond.
questions.hint: Two adjacent carbons form the alkyne.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: From the numbers, a Suzuki coupling of an aryl boronic acid with an aryl halide forms how many new carbon-carbon bonds between the two fragments?
questions.explanation: The coupling joins the two aryl groups through a single new carbon-carbon bond at the positions originally bearing boron and halogen.
questions.hint: One new biaryl bond is formed.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: From the numbers, how many resonance contributors place negative charge on ring carbons in phenoxide?
questions.explanation: Phenoxide has three ring-based contributors placing negative charge at the two ortho positions and the para position, in addition to the contributor with charge on oxygen.
questions.hint: Ortho, para, and the other ortho give three.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: From the numbers, hydrolysis of one mole of an aryl diazonium salt releases how many moles of nitrogen gas?
questions.explanation: The diazonium group contains two nitrogen atoms that leave together as one molecule of nitrogen gas, so one mole of diazonium releases one mole of N2.
questions.hint: The two nitrogens form one N2 molecule.

questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups at the two ortho positions and the para position can stabilize the Meisenheimer intermediate, but counting distinct positions ortho and para gives three possible sites; if a single nitro is considered, the relevant resonance-stabilizing positions are the two ortho sites and the para site, so the count is three when all are substituted; here we take the count of ortho positions as two for this item.
questions.hint: Consider the ortho positions available for stabilization.

questions.explanation: Benzyne has an additional pi bond between two adjacent ring carbons, so exactly two carbons form the strained triple bond.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why is phenol more acidic than cyclohexanol?

answer.exemplar: Deprotonated phenol gives phenoxide, whose negative charge is delocalized by resonance into the aromatic ring at the ortho and para positions, spreading charge and stabilizing the anion; cyclohexoxide has no such conjugation and bears a localized negative charge on oxygen, so it is less stable and its parent alcohol is less acidic.

questions.explanation: Resonance delocalization stabilizes phenoxide. questions.hint: No conjugation in cyclohexoxide.

questions.stem: Explain the following: why must electron-withdrawing groups be ortho or para for SNAr?

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why can benzyne formation lead to substitution at the carbon next to the original halogen?

answer.exemplar: Elimination of a proton adjacent to the leaving group produces a symmetric benzyne whose triple bond spans the original halogen carbon and its neighbor; the nucleophile can add to either carbon of that triple bond, so after protonation the substituent may end up on the neighboring carbon rather than the original one, giving cine substitution.

questions.explanation: The triple bond spans two carbons, either can be attacked. Elimination of a proton adjacent to the leaving group produces a symmetric benzyne whose triple bond spans the original halogen carbon and its neighbor; the nucleophile can add to either carbon of that triple bond, so after protonation the substituent may end up on the neighboring carbon rather than the original one, giving cine substitution.
questions.hint: Symmetric intermediate gives mixed products.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: what are the key steps of the Suzuki catalytic cycle?

answer.exemplar: The palladium catalyst undergoes oxidative addition into the aryl halide bond, then ligand exchange with the boron-derived aryl group from the boronic acid activated by base, and finally reductive elimination forms the new aryl-aryl bond and regenerates the palladium(0) catalyst.

questions.explanation: Oxidative addition, transmetalation, reductive elimination. questions.hint: Base activates the boron partner.

questions.stem: Discuss the reasoning: why is phenol more acidic than cyclohexanol?

answer.exemplar: Deprotonated phenol gives phenoxide, whose negative charge is delocalized by resonance into the aromatic ring at the ortho and para positions, spreading charge and stabilizing the anion; cyclohexoxide has no such conjugation and bears a localized negative charge on oxygen, so it is less stable and its parent alcohol is less acidic.
